sources.title: When will Modern Warfare 4 be on Game Pass?
sources.text: COD: MW4 will be on Game Pass, but not at launch Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 (2026) will not be on Xbox Game Pass at launch, which may came as a point of frustration to those COD fans who were hoping that the company's involvement with Microsoft would mean a day-one Game Pass availability. However, that doesn't mean that it's not coming at some point in the future, as I'll lay out the details below. According to an official press release from the development team, Modern Warfare 4 is not going to be available on Xbox Game Pass until "Holiday 2027," roughly one year after its initial launch and release. Further details about exactly when in the year that will be are currently not available, but either way players can expect a long wait if they're dependant on Game Pass and don't want to purchase a copy for themselves. MW4 will still be available to buy on Xbox from its initial launch date of October 23, 2026, but not on the Game Pass subscription service. If you want an alternative until then, there are still a multitude of Call of Duty games currently available on Xbox Game Pass to download as part of the service, going all the way back to Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War from 2020. Alternatively, if you're less brand-loyal and just want to find an online military shooter to experience with friends, Battlefield 6 is also available for free on Game Pass. © GamesRadar+. sources.title: 8 Call of Duty Games Still Missing from Game Pass
sources.text: The franchise has slipped from its lofty perch in recent years, but there was a time when the launch of a new Call of Duty game was a huge event. The anticipation was never quite on the level of Grand Theft Auto 6 , but the series reliably mattered in a way that many other games did not. When Microsoft purchased Activision, some of us assumed we wouldn’t have to wait long before being able to play all of those classic games on Xbox Game Pass. Why else would Microsoft drop that kind of money on the company, if not to leverage its library of classics? But Call of Duty has made only a weak showing on the subscription service since then, with many of its most iconic games still available only for purchase. With Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launching Oct. 23, here are eight Call of Duty games somehow still missing from Game Pass. We’d love to see them get added soon. After Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 , it was unclear how the franchise might top itself. Then came Call of Duty: Black Ops , with an energetic campaign that included outrageous moments such as an attempted assassination of Fidel Castro. Some of the most memorable characters in the franchise experienced a thrilling campaign, and that was just for starters. Without Black Ops , we never would have been introduced to the Nuketown map so many of us know and love from multiplayer deathmatch. The game’s absence from Game Pass is an injustice. World at War once again told a compelling story set in World War 2, like most of the franchise entries up to that point, but that’s not why most players remember it fondly. Rather, they recall the zombies mode, which developer Treyarch introduced to the overall franchise with sufficient success that it quickly became a standard component in future titles. Players worked to cooperate against increasingly powerful waves of invading zombies, rushing from one site to another and struggling to survive against the endless horde. If you love fighting zombies in Call of Duty, you owe that mode to this one great game, which is sadly missing from Game Pass. And if you want more World War 2 action of a more recent vintage, there’s always 2017’s Call of Duty: WW2 . There’s a popular meme you might have seen: “Press F to pay respects.” The familiar line comes from Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare . Early in the campaign, wounded during a recent military operation and now missing one arm, you attend the funeral of a fallen comrade. As you look over the coffin, text prompts you to press a button to grieve. Also present at that funeral: Jonathan Irons, the father of the slain soldier. Voiced by Kevin Spacey, Irons plays a pivotal role in a story that explores the contentious relationship between private enterprise and the United States government. It’s an intriguing tale, over-the-top in the way some of the best Call of Duty campaigns so often were, even if it occasionally feels contrived. Modern players are missing out on an experience that’s still worth having. Many players associated Infinity Ward with the best Call of Duty had to offer, even though there were three studios working on the series. Following the very noisy exit of Vince Zampella and Jason West in 2010, the remaining team had to work hard to prove they still had the creative juice necessary to build something special. Call of Duty: Ghosts was the result of their effort. Co-developed with Neversoft ( Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater ) and Raven Software, the game suffered from slower pacing and less interesting maps, but still managed to pack in some of the high-octane sequences for which the franchise is known. Although it’s not remembered as a high point for the series, it provided a solid experience that today’s players can still enjoy a great deal, provided they keep their expectations in check. Call of Duty: Black Ops 2 remains one of the most ambitious games in the series to date, offering spectacular multiplayer modes that gave players better control of their loadouts. Its maps were some of the very best, including Raid, Hijacked, and Slums, which players happily ran through time after time. The zombies mode was more ambitious than before, with Mob of the Dead and Origins DLC providing additional zombie maps on top of the ones that shipped on the disc. Black Ops 2 featured a branching narrative with multiple endings, allowing players to decide who lived and died as the team went up against Raul Menendez, one of the most believable villains in franchise history. It also imagined life in 2025, more than a decade after the game’s release date. Overall, the title is a high point for the franchise. It’s a minor tragedy that newer players have no idea what they’ve been missing. Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare had massive battles. In space. It had advanced technology and the firefights you know and love, this time with zero gravity. In space. And it had a compelling, surprisingly intimate plot featuring the voice talents of Brian Bloom and Kit Harington. They probably didn’t record them in space, even if it sounded like it. Besides all of that, some copies of the game shipped with Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered as a bonus, which made a good thing even better. For me and some other players, it was the last time a new Call of Duty game felt like a proper event that was not to be missed. The game’s continued absence from the Game Pass lineup is a real disappointment. A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later. If you say “No Russian” to Call of Duty players of a certain age, they’ll immediately know just what you mean, perhaps even if they didn’t play the original Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 . The scene where that pivotal phrase was uttered ranks among the most memorable ever featured in a first-person shooter. At the time, it was preceded by a warning to let players know they were about to go to a very dark place. But that scene – and the game as a whole – were a welcome gut-punch i

stories.title: Sega and Creative Assembly remove Total War: Shogun 2 remaster from sale as it "falls short of both your expectations and our own standards"
stories.summary: Sega and Creative Assembly have temporarily withdrawn Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition from sale in response to concerns about AI upscaling and other performance issues. Read more

sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Sega and Creative Assembly remove Total War: Shogun 2 remaster from sale as it "falls short of both your expectations and our own standards"
sources.text: Recently launched title has received overwhelmingly negative reviews on Steam, with players citing AI upscaling and performance issues Sega and Creative Assembly have temporarily withdrawn Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition from sale in response to concerns about AI upscaling and other performance issues. Since its October 13 launch, the remaster has received overwhelmingly negative reviews on Steam. Players have reported that assets such as unit cards and new cutscenes display AI-generated features , including extra fingers and armor merging into characters' bodies. As described on Steam , the "underlying graphics technology has been brought to modern standards to take advantage of new methods in rendering," resulting in improved graphics and textures. In response, both companies issued a joint statement acknowledging that the game "has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards." "We've seen your feedback, comments, and reviews. We agree that the current experience is not where it needs to be." "As a result we are working with platform holders to temporarily remove the game from sale and to reinstate the original game while we investigate the issues. Existing owners will still be able to access and play the game." "We are working closely with our development partner to identify the causes of these problems, deliver improvements, and ensure Shogun 2 – Complete Edition meets the quality standards players expect from Total War." Earlier this year, Sega faced criticism for its use of generative AI in Crazy Taxi: World Tour. The game's Steam page included a generative AI disclaimer, which clarified that Sega uses the technology "as a support tool for developers, aiming to provide better content to our users and enable developers to focus more on creative tasks." "We have used such generative AI support tools during development of Crazy Taxi: World Tour. No AI was used in reference to the performers in game." In a statement to Game Informer , Sega clarified that generative AI was "used to support our teams during the development of background assets" and that "assets generated were still subject to review by the development team."

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: The Shogun 2 remaster is so bad, Sega is removing it from sale and bringing back the original
sources.text: Sega admits Shogun 2 - Complete Edition "has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards," so it's going back to the drawing board. Just two days after the disastrous release of Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition, Sega says it is removing the game from sale and putting the original back until it gets things sorted out. Which brings us to now: After two days of silence, Sega has finally made a move: It says "the current experience is not where it needs to be," and is thus "working with platform holders to remove the game from sale and to reinstate the original game while we investigate the issues." Anyone who purchased Shogun 2 - Complete Edition will still have access to it, but how (or if) Sega will enable them to go back to playing the original version wasn't clarified. Pulling Shogun 2 - Complete Edition from sale and restoring the original is obviously the right move, and today's message promises improvements to the game to bring it more in-line with expectations, so hopefully we'll see some of the more glaring bugs and QoL issues resolved. But all of this is still a very bad look for Creative Assembly, which has had something of an up-and-down history with its games and players over the years. It's a particular shame coming so soon after the company's successful launch of the Lords of the End Times expansion for Total War: Warhammer, which has been widely praised. The announcement of Total War: Warhammer 40k also has a lot of RTS fans, and WH40K sickos, very excited, and nonsense like this really takes the wind out of those sails: If Shogun 2 - Complete Edition allowed out the door in this condition, how are fans supposed to expect better in the future? A few fans have also pointed out that in 2024, Sega's Aegis-CWA union accused the company of outsourcing Q&A and some localization services, resulting in the layoffs of 61 people. If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement. Sega is removing Total War: Shogun 2 — Complete Edition from storefronts following a disastrous launch where users complained about issues like bugs and upscaling that appears to have been done by AI. Complete Edition , a remaster of the 2011 strategy game, launched on Tuesday, and it bundled the main game and all of its DLC with promised upgrades including “improved visuals,” “1440p and 4K UI scaling,” and modernized controls. It has an “Overwhelmingly Negative” rating on Steam , where it has already been pulled, and posts on Reddit showcase artwork that users believe AI messed up. “We’re aware that Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards,” Sega and developer Creative Assembly wrote in a post . “We’ve seen your feedback, comments, and reviews. We agree that the current experience is not where it needs to be.” The two companies say they will “reinstate the original game,” and existing owners will “still be able to access ” Complete Edition . Sega and Creative Assembly say that they are “working closely with our development partner to identify the causes of these problems, deliver improvements, and ensure Shogun 2 - Complete Edition meets the quality standards players expect from Total War.” A studio called Mataboo is also listed as a developer for the game on Steam, and Mataboo highlights its work on the game on its website .

stories.title: The Live-Action Cyberpunk 2077 Movie Won't Retrace the Game's Steps, CD Projekt Confirms
stories.summary: CD Projekt Red has finally spoken up about the live-action Cyberpunk 2077 movie. The company said it doesn’t want to do a 1:1 adaptation of the game, instead telling a new story within the same universe.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: The Live-Action Cyberpunk 2077 Movie Won't Retrace the Game's Steps, CD Projekt Confirms
sources.text: CD Projekt Red has finally spoken up about the live-action Cyberpunk 2077 movie . The company said it doesn’t want to do a 1:1 adaptation of the game, instead telling a new story within the same universe. "At this point, we can only say that we definitely don't want to make a film adaptation of the game," co-CEO Michał Nowakowski told Polish outlet PAP Biznes , via GamesRadar . "We want to tell a story in the world of Cyberpunk, but it won't be a one-to-one translation of the game's story." The Cyberpunk movie is being created in partnership with Parmount, now under the Skydance banner after the recent merger . The film will be produced by Lorenzo di Bonaventura, of live-action Transformers fame. It’ll be interesting to see how far the movie strays from the game, which featured a freelance mercenary called V who put a mysterious computer chip in their brain and ended up haunted by the digital ghost of Keanu Reeves’ Johnny Silverhand. I’d personally love them to go back, get Reeves back in, and tell Silverhand’s story before he ended up stuck in a chip. Of course, the Cyberpunk universe — created by tabletop RPG designer Mike Pondsmith — is wide enough to tell a range of original stories. It’s fertile soil for pulling at themes of identity, autonomy, and the self as a ship of theseus to be modified and reprinted. It sounds like a similar approach the company took to anime. Cyberpunk: Edgerunners feels like a faithful multimedia project within the world CDPR created — featuring locations and characters from the game world — but it tells a fresh story about original characters in its dystopian posthuman hellscape. The Studio Trigger-led anime series is back on Netflix this month when Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2 launches on October 20. Check out the IGN interview with the creators of Edgerunners for the lowdown. CD Projekt also recently announced that work has officially begun on Project Hadar , its first game in its own original universe. The company has previously only played in the worlds of others, with The Witcher based on novels and Cyberpunk based on a tabletop RPG. Elsewhere in CD Project Land, The Witcher 3 just got a remaster on consoles and PC, which saw the iconic RPG get a makeover. There were some issues with the new visuals, particularly heavy bloom in The Witcher 3 remaster , but CDPR was on the case quickly. And of course, Cyberpunk 2 is in the works, although it feels years away. Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

sources.title: The Cyberpunk 2077 movie won't be 'a film adaptation of the game,' CD Projekt chief says
sources.text: The game is great, but CD Projekt wants to tell a new story. We learned last week that a Cyberpunk 2077 movie is in the works , an announcement I used mainly to talk about a completely different cyberpunk movie starring Keanu Reeves as a guy named Johnny who's having a bad week. Now we've got a bit more insight into what CD Projekt Red has in mind for the film, and it's possible that a guy named Johnny may not be involved at all. "Our contract with Anonymous Content expired, and in the meantime, an opportunity arose to establish cooperation with Paramount Pictures," co-CEO Michał Nowakowski told Polish PAP Biznes ( Google translated ), referring to the Cyberpunk 2077 "live action project" that was announced in 2023 and ultimately went nowhere. "We decided that we would conduct a live-action Cyberpunk project in a new formula. "At this point, we can only say that we definitely don't want to make a film adaptation of the game. We want to tell a story in the world of Cyberpunk, but it won't be a one-to-one translation of the game's story." I loved Cyberpunk 2077, and the fact that it featured two Hollywood stars in central roles might make it seem like a natural fit for a direct translation. But I think avoiding that approach is the wiser move: V's story has been told, and trying to replicate it on film only invites unflattering comparisons and criticism. And it's not as though the world of Night City is short of other stories to tell, after all, nor would it be difficult to indirectly tie it to the game through references or cameos, if the urge to do so is really that strong. Remember as well that two of the most successful game-to-screen adaptations, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners and Resident Evil , took their respective underlying settings and made them their own. That's basically what Cyberpunk 2077 is, as far as that goes: A vision of Mike Pondsmith's Cyberpunk tabletop setting, interpreted through the lens of a new timeline. They're all stronger for it, because they allow creators to work within a particular framework without tying them to specifics. sources.name: The Verge Games
sources.title: Big Walk skipped Xbox to boycott Microsoft’s involvement with Israel
sources.text: ‘We’ve made this decision with the belief that meaningful change can be made in the world.’﻿ ‘We’ve made this decision with the belief that meaningful change can be made in the world.’﻿ If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement. Big Walk ’s co-op multiplayer walking adventure has proved popular since launching in August, but Xbox players have been excluded from the fun — and now the game’s creators have explained why. Developer House House said in a blog post that it decided not to release Big Walk on Xbox consoles in accordance with the Palestinian-led BDS (Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions) movement, which has called to boycott Microsoft, including products under the company’s gaming division. Microsoft was named a priority BDS target in June last year over contracts it has with the Israeli military and government , with the boycott specifically calling out Xbox consoles and Game Pass subscriptions, gaming franchises owned by Microsoft, and any gaming accessories produced by the company. Microsoft’s involvement with Israel has also been protested by its own employees , and the company has fired staffers for participating in pro-Palestine demonstrations. Here’s what House House said regarding its participation in the boycott: It has always been our intention for Big Walk to be played by groups of friends, and we know that keeping the game off Xbox runs counter to those intentions. This decision means that some people will miss out on playing Big Walk with their friends, and we understand the disappointment we’re causing. We are disappointed too. We would love for people to be able to play the game on Xbox, but not until Microsoft and/or Xbox have been removed as BDS boycott targets. We’ve made this decision with the belief that meaningful change can be made in the world, that coordinated collective action can confront even the most powerful interests, and that one day, Palestine will be free. Big Walk is playable on Microsoft’s Windows operating system, however, as it’s available to download via Steam . We’ve asked House House why it hasn’t excluded Big Walk from Windows and will update if we hear back.

sources.title: Xbox Ally X 20 vs Xbox Ally X: A wickedly bright OLED screen and frosty temps make for a begrudgingly attractive upgrade for the Asus handheld
sources.text: All that glitters might actually be gold. So, you've seen the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 in all its black and gold glory and wondered if it's worth paying $300 more for it. Well, the answer is 'it really depends on what kind of device you are looking for' and 'how much is a fresh OLED screen worth to you?' Unlike the other ROG 20th anniversary edition bits of Asus gear, the X20 is not about superfluous add-ons (unless you pick up the bundle with XR glasses). You aren't getting a commemorative faceplate here, or extra stickers. You get an OLED screen, TMR thumbsticks, improved thermals, and MicroSD Express compatibility. You also get Impulse triggers, which means they can rumble independently, and the D-Pad can be flicked around to make the corners more or less pronounced. The screen is perhaps the biggest sell here, with its 1400 HDR-certified display going up to a peak brightness of 1,400 nits. As I found in my review , it's so sizzlingly bright at points that I looked at the sun in Cyberpunk 2077 while lying in bed one night and actually winced. Check out the full differences below. 1x USB4 Type-C with DP 2.1 / PD 3.0 / TB 4 compatible 1x USB4 Type-C with DP 2.1 / PD 3.0 / TB 4 compatible In a handful of games and productivity apps (35 W plugged in) With both devices featuring the same chip and memory, you can expect more or less the same performance. In my testing, I got lower Metro performance and worse 1% lows in F1 25, but better performance in Horizon Zero Dawn, Cyberpunk 2077 and 3DMark, so the framerate differences overall just about balance out. I also noticed the X20 never went above 49 watts, which means I would feel more comfortable cranking up the wattage. It helps that its thermals are much improved. Recorded in HW Info whilst performing gaming benchmarks (35 W plugged in) The X20 comes with a refined new thermal cooling system, and it's more than just a marketing term. I recorded temps up to 17 °C cooler compared to the previous model, and even in long gaming sessions, I couldn't manage to push the system's temp above 80°C with its included wattage modes (between 17 W and 35 W). Importantly, I never felt that heat on my fingers as I played, making it a relatively frosty gaming device. Recorded using PCMark 10's gaming battery life test (25 W) In stress testing gaming benchmarks, the X20 managed 2 hours and 9 minutes in the 25 W gaming mode, and almost 3 hours in the 17 W mode. Importantly, it can get up to 9 hours of indie gaming on the go, in my experience. The standard X model has the exact same size battery, so you can expect a similar battery life, though our testing saw it perform a little under the X20. The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products Though you're getting similar performance figures, the day-to-day use of the Ally X20 is superior from my experience. The screen is gorgeous and super bright, all the buttons feel superb under the fingers, it's super quiet (unless you want it to be loud), and it looks phenomenal. As well as all of this, those frosty temps mean you can shove up the wattage if you want, or just have a ton of headroom to avoid throttling in the future. I would really struggle to want to spend over $1,000 on any gaming handheld right now, but if I were flush with cash, I would be majorly tempted to pop the X20 in my basket. If you already have the Xbox Ally X, I wouldn't recommend spending another $1,300 to get a better screen, thermals and TMR sticks (plus some little extras). If, however, you're deciding between the two, I can say that the new additions are very welcome and make for a refined, desirable device. If you've got the cash to splash, it's a sweet device. It's just a shame that the memory crisis has killed handheld market prices. 3. sources.title: Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 review
sources.text: Asus' 20th anniversary edition of the Xbox ROG Ally X is as bougie as the $300 price bump implies. Its additions are very welcome, but that's a lot of cash for a familiar package. PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you. Find out more about how we evaluate games and hardware. The Asus ROG 20th anniversary lineup has been interesting. Black, gold, and indulgent feels like the tagline here, with the Azoth Extreme Edition 20 and ROG Harpe II Extreme Edition 20 containing actual gold, and a fitting price tag to boot. For any criticisms I may have, I don't think you're paying primarily for the branding on the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20, though. You get a new OLED screen which is bigger and brighter than the IPS panel in the standard Xbox Ally X, TMR thumbsticks, refined triggers, a new cooling system, and with that screen comes a snappy 0.2 ms response time. Refined is a good word for the device as a whole. Coming a year later than the last model, the software is smooth and intuitive, and it's easy to swap between Xbox and Windows mode, though it still doesn't feel like a console in practice. For my money, it's the best ROG Ally on the market right now, but the memory crisis has skewed the price of all gaming gear, and the X20 is certainly not the best value as a result. ✅ You want a beefy OLED handheld: OLED handhelds are still fairly niche, and with recent price bumps, I'd pick this over the Legion Go 2 or OneXPlayer's offerings. ✅ You want power on the go: I'd suggest a significantly cheaper handheld if you are after low-intensity games and don't particularly care for big-budget ones. For your Cyberpunks and your Horizons, you will want a Z2 Extreme chip or better to play them at a decent resolution and settings. ❌ You're fine with IPS: $300 more for the X20 over the X is pretty steep, especially if you aren't dying to play on an OLED. ❌ You live in the UK: The pricing on the X20 is not as good value in Britain, with the superior G3-equipped MSI Claw being only £100 more (though no OLED) and the standard Xbox Ally X £400 less. Asus' 20th anniversary edition of the Xbox ROG Ally X is as bougie as the $300 price bump implies. Its additions are very welcome, but that's a lot of cash for a familiar package. 1x USB4 Type-C with DP 2.1 / PD 3.0 / TB 4 compatible 1x USB4 Type-C with DP 2.1 / PD 3.0 / TB 4 compatible The Asus ROG Xbox Ally X20 (or should I say XBOX) is a relatively granular update on the Xbox Ally X . I noticed it immediately when putting the two devices side by side, but when it comes to performance, you're getting identical experiences. They have the same chip, the same memory, the same storage. That's the Ryzen Z2 Extreme, 24 GB LPDDR5X, and 1 TB PCIe 4.0 M.2 2280, respectively. Given you don't get a performance bump, you've gotta really care about the details to consider the X20. Arguably its biggest upgrade is the OLED panel, and it is a beauty. The DisplayHDR True Black 1400 certification isn't just for show, as it pops, appearing both bright and ultra-vibrant. It's also got a bigger screen, which does make the device more immersive, but also larger and chunkier. You can technically upgrade the plain old joysticks in the ROG Xbox Ally X with a TMR module with a bit of know-how, but slapping in your own OLED screen would be very difficult, and I certainly wouldn't trust myself to do such fine electronic surgery. Therefore, I do see value in an upgraded, refined, and pretty older brother of last year's device. It's also got a whole new cooling system for frostier temps. You also get smaller upgrades here, like the ability to pull up and turn the D-Pad to make the corner buttons more or less pronounced, plus greater grooves on the face buttons to stop jagged edges, and a combination of more clicky bumpers and smoother triggers. These all combine to make the X20 feel more thoughtful in approach, and given the price bump, it sort of has to do that. The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products The X20 doesn't come with a charger in the box, which makes sense from an e-waste point of view, but it does mean you will get lacking plugged-in performance without an appropriately speedy charger. For instance, I ran the device at 35 W mode and did some of my benchmarks before realising I wasn't getting the full-fat 35 W mode because my charger wasn't quick enough. Could you say that's my fault for not seeing the low-power pop-up from Asus' software Armoury Crate? Absolutely. Does that mean you may need to pick up a quick charger if you want full-wattage plugged-in performance? Also, absolutely. The box for the X20 also comes with a cardboard stand, which doesn't feel as luxurious as the device itself but is clean, effective, and environmentally conscious. It's a small but decent addition that I've been using consistently since unboxing the device without any problems. There was a brief period when the original Asus ROG Xbox Ally X was the highest-performing gaming handheld money could buy. That was until the launch of the much more expensive MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ CG3EM (catchy name, I know) broke onto the scene. Despite launching a year after the original Xbox Ally X, the X20 sees no difference in power (as it has identical specs), and therefore my performance figures are more or less the same as what Dave got in his review of the standard Xbox Ally X. I got a little less in Metro and a little more in Horizon and Cyberpunk 2077, with lower 1% lows in F1 25. In a handful of games, with upscaling on and off (35 W plugged in) I left the GPU memory budget at 8 GB, flicked the device onto its 35 W Turbo mode, and had a good time in F1 24, Horizon Zero Dawn, and Metro Exodus without any upscaling. sources.title: WWE 2K26 is collaborating with Capcom for a DLC pack adding five WWE wrestlers as Street Fighter action figures
sources.text: The WWE 2K26 X Street Fighter Elite Pack adds new special moves and cosmetic parts WWE 2K26 is getting a special collaboration DLC pack which sees Street Fighter action figures being added to the game. Mattel first launched its WWE Elite Collection X Street Fighter action figures in 2025, which features WWE superstars dressed as Street Fighter characters. To date, there have been four series of these figures, and now a selection of them are being added to the game as playable characters. They’ll be arriving in the WWE 2K26 X Street Fighter Elite Pack, which will be a separate paid DLC pack not included in any existing bundles or premium editions of the game. The pack, which will be available from October 28, contains playable versions of the five following crossover action figures: Rather than simply reskinned versions of the existing wrestlers, each character will have their own entrance music and video, and will have their own movesets featuring Street Fighter special moves including the Shinku Hadoken, Psycho Crusher, Spiral Arrow, Electric Thunder and Shoryuken. As well as the five superstars, the pack will also include 15 extra create-a-superstar parts from numerous Street Fighter characters, including M. Bison, Ryu, Akuma, Vega and Chun-Li. VGCâs WWE 2K26 review called it the best entry in the series to date, but noted that it didnât innovate too much over the 2K25 edition and still had room for improvement. âWWE 2K26 offers another net gain over its predecessor, ensuring the series continues to evolve in a positive direction,â we said. âWhile its new reversal system will initially divide players and the spectre of microtransactions continues to loom over MyFaction, the overall package introduces more quality-of-life features to ensure each of its numerous modes is better than it was last time.â

sources.title: Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World details online content, offline Battle Arena, and Wrangler’s Gauntlet
sources.text: Publisher and developer Square Enix , and developer TOSE have released new information and screenshots for Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World introducing online content, the offline Battle Arena, and the new roguelike mode Wrangler’s Gauntlet. ■ Team Up With Wranglers the World Over and Take on Joint Battles Together! After you progress some way through the story of Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World , you’ll unlock a host of online content. These modes are enabled for cross-platform play, meaning you can enjoy them with anyone, regardless of their chosen gaming system. One of those modes is Online Joint Battles, where you can team up with other wranglers to test your skills against massive monsters together. There are daily quests to try your hand at, as well as special events featuring infamous monsters from across the Dragon Quest series, with fantastic rewards for those able to overcome the challenge! —With three difficulties of regular quests to choose from, you can select the level of challenge that best matches your current party’s strength. —Once you’ve chosen the quest you want to take on, you can start the matching process to find other players. You can also choose to play alone if you wish. —During battle, you can talk with your teammates using a selection of simple preset messages—and you’ll need to communicate if you want to emerge victorious! —When you use healing and support skills on allied parties in battle, you’ll boost your collective Team Bonus. This multiplier increases the damage that everyone can inflict on the enemy and boosts the effectiveness of healing abilities. —Keep an eye out for super-tough Special Quests that feature special monsters. These events regularly come and go, so be sure to give them a try if you’re feeling strong enough. You can earn monster eggs as rewards for completing Online Joint Battles and other challenges. The monsters that hatch forth can then be added to your party! —Eggs come in four colors, and all sorts of monsters can be inside. ■ Connect Online to Access a Wealth of Extra Content! In addition to Online Joint Battles, connecting online allows you to battle against other players in Ranked Matches to improve your global ranking, fight parties that players have uploaded via the Wranglers Society and much more. However, because the online content, such as Online Joint Battles and Ranked Matches, is intended to be a fair test of your monster wrangling skills, the Wrangler’s Spirit ability won’t activate in these game modes. —In Ranked Matches, you compete against other players of a similar ability to yours. There are seven main ranks, from Beginner to Legendary, and the goal is to rise as far you can in the standings. —Every victory rewards you with Ranking Points. Your total at the end of a season determines your rank. Perform well and you might earn promotion to a higher rank, with rewards for doing so! —In Private Matches, you can customize the rules of battle, such as setting the number of rounds or the times you can swap in your reserves. —Head over to the Online Hub, where other players are represented, to participate in the Wranglers Society. By speaking to the wranglers there, you can battle against their parties, so be sure to take your strongest monsters along with you. —Win a battle in the Wranglers Society and you’ll get to spin the roulette wheel to determine your reward, with items, mini medals and other great prizes up for grabs. —The Online Shop has some valuable items for sale. The lineup changes depending on the day of the week and your progress through the story, so check back regularly to see what new stock has come in. ■ The Battle Arena, Where Monster Wranglers Go to Test Their Mettle! In addition to the online content, there’s also a fully offline Battle Arena to enjoy, which Bianca and Nera will discover upon visiting Witherwood Castle. In these contests, you’ll send the monsters you’ve raised into battles that will determine the strongest wrangler in the kingdom. This Battle Arena features both regular battles and joint battles, each with seven difficulty categories from G up to A. With rewards on offer for completing a category, the Battle Arena is the perfect place to test your skills or take a break from adventuring. —In the regular Arena Battles, you have to win all three matches in a category to complete it. Your monsters’ HP and MP will be fully restored between matches, so you can always fight to the max. Once you pay the entry fee, it’s time to start battling! —During battle, you can choose the general tactics you want your monsters to follow. Keep close tabs on how each battle plays out and adjust your tactics accordingly. —In Joint Battles at the arena, you can set the tactics for your main party and your reserves, as well as for the other monster wranglers who fight alongside you. ■ An All-New Roguelike Mode for Extended Replayability! Progress even further through the story and a new challenge will unlock in the Battle Arena called the “Wrangler’s Gauntlet” that will truly test your ability as a monster wrangler! Devised by Scruffy, the Wrangler’s Gauntlet provides you with a selection of monsters that changes each time you attempt the challenge. You must use what you’re given to build a party capable of winning 50 consecutive battles. The monsters you befriend here, and the items you obtain, can’t be taken out on your adventures, but with different starting monsters each time and opponents that change with every new attempt, no two runs are ever the same. The roguelike elements offer a fresh perspective on monster wrangling! —The challenge begins once you receive your monsters from Scruffy. He’ll even tell you which monsters you’ll face off against in the next battle, meaning you can tailor your party to best deal with each different opponent. —After winning a battle, you’ll have the opportunity to strengthen your party. sources.title: Toxic Crusaders ‘Gameplay’ trailer
sources.text: Retroware has released a new gameplay trailer for side-scrolling beat ’em up game Toxic Crusaders . Here is an overview of the game, via its Steam page : When the evil Dr. Killemoff attacks, only one team of hideously deformed creatures of superhuman size and strength stands between him and his plans for global pollution: the Toxic Crusaders, earth’s last, greatest and ugliest hope for survival! The hottest heroes of 1991 return for a radical, radioactive beat ’em up for a new era, featuring awesome action, crushing combos and more toxic waste than you’ll know what to do with! Choose from seven playable characters, including Toxie, No-Zone, Junkyard, Major Disaster and Headbanger (who would technically count as two characters if they could only agree on something)—plus, for the first time, play as Toxie’s musically “gifted” girlfriend Yvonne, and the mother of all mothers, Mrs. Junko, Toxie’s mom! Battle across seven disgusting levels rendered in beautiful full-color pixel art as you defend Tromaville from hordes of Radiation Rangers, mutated thugs and zombie chickens. The odds might be stacked against you but with awesome powers, a winning personality and up to four-player local co-up on your side, the Smogulan Empire’s days are numbered! Take a deep breath and dive deep into an action-packed, pun-filled adventure that drags you kicking and screaming through the wonderful world of Troma. Enjoy cameos from gore-filled classics such as Class of Nuke ‘Em High, Poultrygeist: Night of the Chicken Dead, and Sgt. Kabukiman N.Y.P.D.—reimagined in the Saturday morning cartoon style that made this franchise so unforgettable! Toxic Crusaders is due out for PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series , PlayStation 4 , Xbox One , Switch , and PC via Steam in 2026.

sources.name: Gematsu
sources.title: Heavy Metal Death Can now available for PS5, Xbox Series
sources.text: Survival horror game Heavy Metal Death Can is now available for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series for $17.49, developer Krufs Productions announced. Heavy Metal Death Can first launched for PC via Steam on May 28. Here is an overview of the game, via its Steam page : Heavy Metal Death Can is an old-school survival horror game set on a Swedish Cold War–era submarine. Trapped beneath the ocean, you must fight against the terrifying Sludge which has turned your crew into Zombies. Look for survivors and uncover the truth behind the madness. Classic Survival Horror Emerges from the Depths Heavy Metal Death Can is a retro-inspired survival horror game set on a submarine in an alternate history version of late 70s Sweden. Trapped in the depths of the Norwegian Sea you must fight for survival against the terrifying Sludge which has possessed your crew mates and turned them into horrific zombies. Look for survivors and uncover the truth behind the madness. Step into a claustrophobic, rust-ridden nightmare inspired by genre-defining classics of the PS1 era. With limited ammo, fixed camera angles, and analog dread, every creak of the hull might be your last. Discover the chilling secrets behind the incident on the vessel HMS Domherren. Each corridor reveals fragments of a buried conspiracy… and something not quite human.
